newsitem.title: USA: US Boeing merger approval likely next week.
newsitem.headline: US Boeing merger approval likely next week.

text.p: United States authorities are likely to approve the merger of Boeing and McDonnell Douglas early next week, sources familiar with the situation said Friday.
Federal Trade Commission approval of the $14 billion deal will have few conditions attached to it, those sources said.
The decision will meet a July 1 deadline which is 20 days after the companies submitted their voluminous papers, running into millions of pages, to the FTC.
Such deadlines are often extended by the agreement of both parties, but in this case no extension is expected.
Spokeswomen for the Federal Trade Commission and Boeing had no comment.
Separately, Boeing and McDonnell Douglas have submitted their merger for approval by competition authorities in the European Union.

A source said Boeing and McDonnell Douglas have shown flexibility on the delicate and crucial question of Boeing's exclusive sales agreements with Delta Airlines American Airlines and Continental Airlines.
EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said in the spring the merger could not be approved with those exclusive provider agreements in place.
A spokeswoman for Boeing declined comment about the nature of negotiations with the EU.

Whatever agreement the two sides reach is likely to be completed some time next week. On July, 4 EU competition authorities share their proposed recommendations on the Boeing deal in a closed meeting with competition authorities from the 15 EU nations.
